newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares seen waiting for turn-of-year rally.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares seen waiting for turn-of-year rally.

text.p: The Russian share market is set for a strong rally towards the turn of the year but showed only a few sparks on Tuesday, traders said.
The Russian Trading System ticked up less than one percent to 190.51 on $16.0 million turnover.
"It's got a good feel, but we're not going anywhere," said a London trader for a Western bank.
Shares were seen stagnant for the next two weeks as traders are likely to guard their profits through bonus time but were then expected to pick up.
"The rally will start in the last two weeks of December when the Westerners have been away -- the locals generally mark up prices," said the London trader.
He also predicted shares would gain as much as 25 percent as Westerners entered the market in mid-to-late January.
Bill Browder, managing director of Hermitage Capital Management in Moscow, said money would flow into Russian shares but it would be a stream and not a flood.
Falling interest rates would make government securities less attractive, he said.
Renaissance Capital's Victor Pitaleff, who did not expect any strong movement over the next couple of weeks, said the market as a whole had smoothed out into a tight trading range.
"Prices of second tier shares have evened out and will trade more or less like blue chips," he said.
UES edged up to $0.0833 from $0.0823, which brokers said was in anticipation of an auction of 8.5 percent of UES stock on December 23.
"We have seen big buys and that resumed today," said Pavel Gronbjerg of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Some dealers said Russian firms were also bidding up the stock in expectation of an investor rush for the leading issue, though large Western orders were also seen.
UES preference shares rose to $0.0650 from $0.0637.

Surgutneftegaz, which on Tuesday announced plans to offer American Depositary Receipts for preferred shares, saw those shares tick up to $0.314, down from a daily high of $0.320 but well above Tuesday's close of $0.304.
